project_title: Graphic Novel Script Adapter Needed — Create Polished Sample for Crowdfunding

project_metadata.job_title: Graphic Novel Script Adapter Needed — Create Polished Sample for Crowdfunding
project_metadata.job_description:
I’m looking for a writer experienced in graphic novels, comics, or sequential storytelling to adapt a portion of my completed screenplay into a polished sample script for a future crowdfunding campaign.

This job is for a paid sample only (fixed price: $100). If the sample works well, there will be an opportunity to continue with the full graphic novel script.

What I need:

Adapt a selected section of my screenplay into a comic/graphic novel script format
Break the material into pages, panels, dialogue, captions, and visual direction
Maintain pacing, clarity, and strong visual storytelling
Deliver a clean, professional script sample suitable for showing to artists and potential backers

What I will provide:

The full screenplay
Character notes and tone/style references
The specific scene/sequence to adapt for the sample

Ideal experience:

Comic book or graphic novel writing
Screenplay adaptation
Panel‑by‑panel scripting
Storyboarding or sequential art familiarity (a plus)

This sample will be used to help pitch the project and secure funding. If we’re a good fit, there will be ongoing paid work as the project moves into full production.

Please include relevant writing samples, especially any comic or graphic novel work.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi Jeffrey.

I appreciate the quick reply. I'll try to answer your questions.

1. I imagined that I would start at the beginning and see how far into the
story I could get. However, if there's a section you would prefer I focus
on, I can do that instead.

2. In the folder I shared as a sample, you can see my default script style.
I suggest a panel format for each page. I sometimes note where captions
should be placed, but I mostly let the artist decide where exactly to put
dialogue balloons and so on.

3. Since I'd be adapting your script, my control of pacing and structure
would mostly be about deciding how many panels (or how much page space) to
give each moment. I think those choices should be fairly self-explanatory,
but if you'd like me to explain anything after I've written it I can do so.
Adding explanatory notes would add time to the process and so increase my
rate for the larger project.

I look forward to hearing back from you.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Excellent! Thank you for the response. I am still evaluating all candidates today and will make a decision my end of day (my time). Please let me know if you have any questions.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello Cory,
One final question... how long to complete this sample project?
Thanks!
Jeff

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
If I can start tomorrow, I would aim to get the script back to you on Friday. That would let me put some time between the first and second draft, and also allow time for any questions that might come up.
Thanks,
Cory

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I would like to move forward with your 12-page sample. If you would like to accept please let me know and I will send the contract. The terms are as discussed in our messages. If you have any questions, please let me know. Otherwise, I will send it out shortly. Thanks!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I attached some other files to give you more info. Let me know if you have any questions or need anything else from me. I am available during the day and in a pinch at night. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Excellent. It looks like you've already funded the project, so I'll go ahead and get started on it in the morning, and I'll let you know if any questions come up. (And I'll try to give an update at the end of the day tomorrow, regardless.)

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Here's an update: I've made some good progress today, and worked out a tentative breakdown that gets as far as Tom meeting Apollonia on comic page 12. I may end up deciding that pace is too brisk, if certain beats need more space to breathe--it's something I'll need to figure out as I go.
I have two questions, or rather two thoughts on how to approach the script that I want to check with you:
1.. In a few places I think I want to adapt parts of the scene descriptions into "voice over" caption text.
2\. There are a few short exchanges that I might want to omit for the sake of efficiency and page space. For example, at the bottom of page 23 where Carter tells Tom he's invited to the dinner he attends in the following scene.
I wanted to check whether deviations from the script of that size would be acceptable, or if you want the comic to represent the screenplay line-for-line. Let me know what you think.
Thanks.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hey Cory,
I am giving you carte blanche for this. Since it is a sample piece I will defer to your judgement.
Let me know what you need from me.
Jeff

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Also, a heads-up that I'll be away from my desk for most of the day tomorrow. If you have any questions, I'll get back to you as soon as I can.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Nice work! I will let you know if I need anything else. If you are cool with keeping the contract open a little longer let me know. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Sure! No need to close the job at this point.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello Cory!
Can you quote me your total for 80-85 pages?
Thanks!
Jeff

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi! I'm glad to hear back from you.
May I ask how many episodes/screenplay pages you would want the 85 comic
pages to cover? That will help me figure how much time it would take.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: So the original book was divided into 5 parts. For the first graphic novel I am looking at the first two parts. I can send the files to you later this evening. I am finalizing the production costs and will be launching the crowdfunding on Monday. So if you could get me a quote before that, I would appreciate it. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Thanks. I'll take a look at the files I have, and anything you want to
send, and make some calculations. I'll try to get you the estimate this
evening; otherwise, I'll get it to you on Sunday.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I did some math based on what I wrote already.
To clarify, is it 85 pages of screenplay, or 85 pages of comic? I ended up with a roughly 2:1 ration of screenplay pages to comic pages.
If part 2 is about the same size as the episode 1 I worked with, then parts 1 and 2 would come to about 40-45 comic pages. I think I could price that task at $350 with a timeline of 2 weeks. (If I can reuse 12 pages of the sample script, with perhaps a light revision and reflowing of pages, i could drop that to $275.)
If you want 80-85 comic pages, I can do that too, but I should probably cover more of the story: presumably through episode 3 or 4. For this scope I would propose $675 and a 4-week turnaround ($600 even if reusing the 12 pages of sample script).
Let me know which of these is closer to what you're thinking, and if this works for you.
Thanks,
Cory

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: 85 pages of comic is the current estimate. here are the next two scripts. I think I gave you a version of the novel as well. it is broken up into three sections. that may be a better source than the scripts. take a look and let me know your thoughts.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Also, I am budgeting $1500 for this service so while I appreciate the quote, I feel that this would be more appropriate for your time. Let me know if you have any questions and I will let you know when I have some news. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
In that case, thank you very much. For that rate I will be able to spend some more time on the best way to present everything, rather than relying so closely on the screenplay.

Would you like me to get started on this next week, or should I wait for you to say "go?"

I can commit to scripting 80-85 comic pages. I'll look over the next two episodes and the novel, and work out how much of the story to cover in that space. As I do that, should I pace things with an eye toward eventually scripting the rest of the story? That is, should I aim for something that feels self-contained, or focus on leaving the reader asking, "What's next?"

Thanks,
Cory

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I am posting the listing on Monday. Do you have any objection to using your name as the scripter (or whatever you want to call it) for the project?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
No objection. I prefer to be credited as Corodon Fuller.

You can start the next job as a follow-up to this one (or I can set it up)
if you don't want other bidders.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I will add a milestone, but remember, I am hoping to fund this on Kickstarter. So fingers crossed.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: So this part of the job is contingent on the Kickstarter funding?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Yes. I believe I was clear about that. Does this change your involvement?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
My understanding was that this would be used to secure crowdfunding, not
that it the funding for it wasn't yet secure.
Unfortunately I can't take spec work over this site, and this is too big a
job for me to do that even if I could.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I apologize for any confusion. I am hoping to get funding. The sample that I paid for was part of that. If the campaign is successful, I will be moving forward with the project. I am not asking you for any work yet. But if you would like to withdraw, please let me know ASAP.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I may have misunderstood, and I apologize if I was short. I will be happy
to go ahead with the work once the funding is ready, and I can hold off on
starting while you run the Kickstarter campaign.
Best of luck, and I'll look forward to hearing that it was successful.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: All good! I will share a link when its up. If you have a short bio I can add that to the listing. Up to you.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
This is the link. The pre-launch is tomorrow, and the full launch is Wednesday. Please feel free to share. 
<https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/theothermonster/the-other-monster-volume-one>

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Awesome. Thanks, and best of luck with it.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: So, things did not go as well as I had hoped. Thanks for your participation and efforts. I will be closing the contract tomorrow. Of course I will leave you a top-notch review. I appreciate your time.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I'm sorry to hear that. It's been a pleasure working with you, and I wish you the best in your next projects. Please keep me in mind if you have need of a writer again.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hey Cory,
The artist scheduled for this project has offered to create more artwork gratis and wants me to run the kickstarter again. So if you don't mind, I will keep the contract open. I will update you when anything changes.
Jeff

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
No problem. Let me know if you need anything else, and I'll keep an eye
out.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello Cory,
Not much of an update at the moment. I am looking at a timeline of getting this launched again by the end of July. 
Thanks again for your help!
Jeff

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Well, this project is on hold indefinitely. I am going to end the contract. I appreciate your time and will leave you excellent feedback. If you ever need anything let me know.
